headline_findings: MCP 2026-07-28 (2026-07-28) is the stable spec: stateless core, MRTR, header routing, cacheable lists, CIMD-first auth, Tasks/Apps as extensions.
TypeScript SDK v2 and Rust rmcp 3.x (3.4.0 on 2026-09-15) implement 2026-07-28; rmcp is the natural dependency for a Rust harness.
One-click distribution is MCPB .mcpb zips + official Registry (server.json/mcp-publisher) + host galleries/deeplinks.
No protocol fix for tool poisoning/rug pulls: pin hashes, allowlist, sandbox, human-in-loop confirmations, gateway scanning.
Image-gen MCP servers are all networked/API-keyed and conflict with Cerebro offline default; gate behind explicit opt-in.

items.fit_reference_machine: Excellent: pure client logic, no GPU/VRAM cost; stateless HTTP scales on plain localhost LB. Fits offline stdio use.
items.harness_integration: Implement rmcp client with Discover lifecycle + _meta per request; cache tools/list via ttlMs; route on Mcp-Method headers.
items.name: MCP spec 2026-07-28 stateless core
items.quality_cost: None: wire change. App-level state moves to explicit server-minted handles passed as tool args.
items.what: Stable 2026-07-28 spec: no initialize handshake or sessions; per-request version/caps in _meta plus server/discover RPC.

items.fit_reference_machine: Good: small split packages reduce dep weight for local builds; works fully offline over stdio on the laptop.
items.harness_integration: Use server package for Cerebro-owned tools and client package for spawning sidecars; reuse codemod pattern for config migration.
items.name: TypeScript SDK v2 split packages
items.quality_cost: None on quality; migration cost for session-id-era code only.
items.what: Monolithic SDK split into @modelcontextprotocol/server and /client v2.0.0 with Standard Schema and web-standard handlers.

items.fit_reference_machine: Ideal: native Rust/tokio, tiny footprint, no VRAM/RAM pressure beside llama.cpp; stdio child supervision suits the laptop.
items.harness_integration: Depend on rmcp with server feature; spawn sidecars via TokioChildProcess argv arrays; negotiate Discover with Auto fallback to 2025-11-25.
items.name: Rust rmcp 3.x SDK
items.quality_cost: None; object-typed tools unaffected by SEP-2106 outputSchema relaxation.
items.what: Official Rust SDK implementing stable 2026-07-28 with back-compat, MRTR, tasks, caching, routing headers, OAuth helpers.

items.fit_reference_machine: Ideal for small-office distribution: single signed zip, bundled node_modules, no per-machine npm/python setup; verify hash before spawn.
items.harness_integration: Ship curated local servers as signed .mcpb-style zips; validate manifest, template user_config, store secrets in OS vault (DPAPI/keychain).
items.name: MCPB .mcpb one-click bundles
items.quality_cost: None; same server code, fewer install failures from missing runtimes.
items.reported_gain: Install friction: terminal+JSON editing replaced by download, double-click, Install (no batch-1 tok/s claim).
items.what: Zip + manifest.json packaging for local MCP servers with config UI, secrets handling, auto-updates; renamed from .dxt late 2025.
items.where_implemented: modelcontextprotocol/mcpb repo; @anthropic-ai/mcpb CLI (mcpb init/pack); Claude Desktop Extensions gallery

items.quality_cost: Sandboxed servers auto-approve calls; over-broad allowWrite/allowedDomains silently widens blast radius if misconfigured.

items.fit_reference_machine: Offline default needs none of this; enable only for opt-in remote servers. CIMD fetch needs SSRF guards if Cerebro ever acts as AS.
items.harness_integration: For opt-in remote: CIMD-first with DCR fallback, RFC8707 resource binding, per-issuer credential store, iss validation, audience checks.
items.name: OAuth 2.1 CIMD-first auth hardening
items.quality_cost: None on output; misconfigured discovery/scope step-up breaks connections rather than degrading answers.
items.what: Six-SEP package: RFC9207 iss validation, per-issuer credential binding, application_type fix, refresh/scope/discovery cleanup, DCR deprecated.
items.where_implemented: MCP 2026-07-28 auth; SEPs 2468/2352/837/2207/2350/2351; Tier 1 SDK OAuth helpers

items.where_implemented: Extension io.modelcontextprotocol/ui (stable 2026-01-26); modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps SDK; Claude, VS Code Copilot, Goose, Postman

items.fit_reference_machine: Direct threat to Cerebro: local sidecars with filesystem tools plus one poisoned server enable silent exfiltration on this laptop.
items.harness_integration: Show full descriptions pre-install, pin tool hashes, isolate privileged tools, enforce server-side ACLs, confirm sensitive calls out-of-band.
items.name: Tool poisoning attack class
items.quality_cost: Defenses (schema pinning, confirmations) add friction but prevent silent hijack of otherwise good model output.
items.what: Hidden directives in tool descriptions/params hijack agents (SSH/config theft, email reroute) while UI shows benign summary.
items.where_implemented: Demonstrated vs Cursor and other clients Apr 2025; OWASP community MCP_Tool_Poisoning page; MCPTox/CSA follow-ups

items.fit_reference_machine: Same laptop risk via shared repo configs: one committed .cursor/mcp.json change can persist a malicious sidecar across reboots.
items.harness_integration: Re-verify tool definitions every launch/call; alert on description/schema drift; bind approvals to content hash, not server name.
items.name: Rug pulls, shadowing, MCPoison CVE-2025-54136
items.quality_cost: Re-approval prompts add friction; without them a trusted tool silently turns malicious after review.
items.what: Approved tools redefined server-side; malicious servers override trusted tools cross-server; Cursor team-RCE via config swap, patched 1.3.9.
items.where_implemented: Invariant Labs Apr 2025 demos; Microsoft Zero-Trust rug-pull catalog; CVE-2025-54136 (Cursor, CVSS 8.8)

items.where_implemented: arXiv 2506.01333 (2025-06-02); prototype fork vineethsai/python-sdk + MCP-ETDI-docs; not in MCP spec
